examples.en: I laughed a lot when I heard that story.
I listened to my friend's story until late at night.
The story of that movie is really interesting.
The child loves old stories.
Shall we talk for a bit?

explain: 말할 때는 ‘이야기’를 ‘얘기’로 줄여서 자주 말해요. ‘이야기하다’는 ‘말하다’보다 길게 주고받는 느낌이라서 ‘친구하고 이야기해요’는 자연스럽지만 ‘한 단어를 이야기해요’는 어색해요.

phrases.en: that's a different story
phrases.nuance_ko: 조건이 바뀌어서 생각이나 대답도 바뀔 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: used when the conditions change and so does your opinion or answer

dict_examples.ko: 그들이 싸우게 된 이야기를 듣고 시시비비를 가려 주었다.
dict_examples.en: I heard how they came to fight and helped settle who was right.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 이 아저씨를 나는 무척 좋아했다. 그것은 아저씨가 이따금 내게 들려주는 전쟁 이야기 때문이기도 하였다.
dict_examples.en: I really liked this man. Partly it was because of the war stories he sometimes told me.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 나를 의식하고 하는 이야기 같기도 하고 혼자 중얼거리는 것 같기도 했다.
dict_examples.en: It seemed both like something said with me in mind and like he was muttering to himself.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: In speech, ‘이야기’ is often shortened to ‘얘기’. ‘이야기하다’ suggests a longer back-and-forth than ‘말하다’, so ‘친구하고 이야기해요’ sounds natural, but ‘한 단어를 이야기해요’ sounds odd.

p.n: 스토리 points to the plot as a designed structure.

examples.en: I really have to get in touch with the teacher.
My friend hasn't been in touch today.

examples.ko: 나중에 연락 주세요. 번호는 여기 있어요.
examples.en: Please contact me later. My number is here.

explain: ‘연락’은 [열락]으로 소리 나요. ‘연락하다’, ‘연락이 오다/없다’처럼 쓰고, 윗사람에게는 ‘연락을 드리다’, 부탁할 때는 ‘연락 주세요’라고 해요. 전화, 문자, 메일 모두 ‘연락’이에요.

phrases.en: I contact my friend on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: ‘연락’에 ‘-해요’를 붙이면 동사가 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -해요 to 연락 makes it a verb.

phrases.en: Please contact me when you have time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대방에게 연락해 달라고 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to ask someone to contact you.

phrases.en: I haven't heard from my friend since yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기다리는 연락이 오지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when an expected message hasn't come.

dict_examples.en: Please contact us if anything comes up.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: I'll get in touch with you again next time.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역
국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 연락 is pronounced [열락]. It's used as 연락하다, 연락이 오다/없다; to a superior say 연락을 드리다, and to ask someone to get in touch say 연락 주세요. Calls, texts, and emails all count as 연락.

dis.h: noun: a call or message from someone
gh: verb: to get in touch with someone

p.n: Noun versus verb; 연락하다 would need a different sentence frame.

examples.en: I graduate from university this year.
After I graduate, I'm going to work at a company.
My younger sibling graduated from high school last year.
After I graduate, I want to rest a bit.

examples.ko: 졸업하기 전에 꼭 해 보고 싶은 일이 있어요.
examples.en: There's something I really want to try before I graduate.
When I graduate, I'll go back to my hometown.

explain: 반대는 '입학하다'예요. 보통 '대학교를 졸업하다'처럼 '을/를'과 함께 써요. '어느 학교 졸업했어요?'처럼 물을 수 있고, 행사는 '졸업식', 사람은 '졸업생'이에요.

phrases.en: I graduated from university last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 졸업한 일을 말하는 과거형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form for having already graduated.

phrases.en: My younger sibling's graduation ceremony is next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 졸업하는 날의 행사를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The ceremony held when people graduate.

phrases.en: After I graduate, I'll go on a trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 졸업한 뒤에 할 일을 이어서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to link what you'll do after graduating.

explain_en: Its opposite is '입학하다' (to enter a school). It normally takes '을/를', as in '대학교를 졸업하다'. You can ask '어느 학교 졸업했어요?', and the ceremony is '졸업식' and the person a '졸업생'.

examples.en: I misheard.
I took the wrong bus.
I pressed the wrong phone number.
I wrote my friend's name wrong.
A package came to me by mistake.

explain: ‘잘못’은 동사 바로 앞에 와서 ‘틀리게’라는 뜻을 더해요: 잘못 탔어요, 잘못 들었어요. 띄어 쓴 ‘잘 못해요’는 ‘잘하지 못해요’라는 뜻이라서 달라요. ‘잘못했어요’는 내 실수를 인정하는 사과예요.

phrases.example: 서두르세요. 잘못하면 비행기를 놓칠 수도 있어요.
phrases.en: if things go wrong; you could end up…
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 일이 생길 수도 있다고 걱정하거나 경고할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: used to worry or warn that something bad could happen
phrases.en_equiv: if things go wrong; you could end up…

dict_examples.ko: 소년은 길을 잘못 들어서 한참 헤맸다.
dict_examples.en: The boy took a wrong turn and wandered around for a long time.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 심판은 규칙을 잘못 적용하여 비난을 받았다.
dict_examples.en: The referee was criticized for applying the rules wrongly.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: Learning something the wrong way is worse than not learning it at all.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: Placed right before a verb, ‘잘못’ means doing it the wrong way: 잘못 탔어요 (took the wrong one), 잘못 들었어요 (misheard). With a space, ‘잘 못해요’ means ‘I'm not good at it’ — a different thing. ‘잘못했어요’ is an apology that admits your mistake.

dis.h: fault or blame; doing something wrong
gh: careless slip, not done on purpose
formal error from confusion or misunderstanding

p.n: 잘못 means being at fault. 실수 means an unintended slip.

en: to be fun; to be enjoyable

examples.en: This drama is really fun.
If you know any fun books, please recommend one.
Studying Korean is getting more fun.
Was that game fun yesterday?
That story is really interesting!
I signed up because it seemed more fun than I expected.

explain: '재미있다'의 준말로, 말할 때 더 자주 써요. 반대는 '재미없다'이고 '재밌없다'는 틀린 말이에요. '웃기다'는 웃음이 나오는 일에만 쓰지만, '재밌다'는 웃기지 않아도 흥미롭고 즐거울 때 써요.

phrases.en: This movie is really fun.
phrases.nuance_ko: '재밌다'의 본말이에요. 글이나 말 모두에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The full form of 'jaemitda', used in both writing and speech.

phrases.en: My grandfather told me an interesting story.
phrases.nuance_ko: '재밌는'으로 바꿔서 뒤의 명사를 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: '재밌는' modifies the noun that follows.

phrases.example: 어제 친구와 노는 게 정말 재밌었어요.
phrases.en: Hanging out with my friend yesterday was really fun.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 지난 일을 말하는 과거형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form for something that already happened.

explain_en: It is the contracted form of '재미있다' and is used more in speech. The opposite is '재미없다'; '재밌없다' is wrong. '웃기다' is only for things that make you laugh, but '재밌다' also covers things that are simply interesting and enjoyable.

gh: full standard form; fun or interesting

p.n: Same meaning. 재미있다 is the full form and a bit more neutral in writing.

en: to order; to place an order

examples.en: I ordered jajangmyeon at the Chinese restaurant.
Excuse me, would you like to order?

examples.ko: 인터넷으로 주문한 옷이 아직 안 왔어요.
examples.en: The clothes I ordered online haven't arrived yet.
If you order through the app, it arrives faster.
I always order only iced Americano.
You have to order at the kiosk first.

explain: 음식뿐 아니라 인터넷 쇼핑, 물건 제작에도 써요. 음식은 '짜장면 시켰어요'처럼 '시키다'로도 말하는데 일상 대화에서 자연스러워요. 가게 쪽에서는 '주문을 받다', 손님 쪽에서는 '주문을 하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I placed my order first at the cafe.
phrases.nuance_ko: '주문하다'를 띄어 쓴 말이에요. 손님 쪽에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The spaced-out form of 'jumunhada', used from the customer's side.

phrases.en: The clerk takes the customer's order.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게 쪽에서 주문을 받을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the shop's side when taking an order.

phrases.en: Let's order pizza and eat it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식을 주문할 때 일상 대화에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly used in daily speech when ordering food.

explain_en: Order goods or food — neutral, shops and cafes (커피를 주문해요) It is used not only for food but also for online shopping and custom-made goods. For food, '시키다' is also natural in daily talk, as in '짜장면 시켰어요'. The shop 'takes' an order (주문을 받다) and the customer 'places' it (주문을 하다).

gh: casual order of food; also make someone do
business places a stock order with supplier

p.n: The replacement is more casual and colloquial.

t90.ax: Excuse me, would you like to order?

examples.en: Yesterday evening I watched a movie with a friend.
My head has been hurting since last evening.
Did you watch the nine o'clock news last evening?
Last evening it rained a lot.
I'm really sorry about what happened last evening.
Up until last evening the weather was fine.

explain: '어젯밤'은 잠자기 전 늦은 시간의 느낌이 강하고, '어제저녁'은 저녁 식사 무렵처럼 조금 이른 시간을 말할 때 잘 어울려요. 뒤에 '에'를 붙이거나 생략해도 돼요. '어제 저녁'처럼 띄어 쓴 형태로도 많이 봐요.

phrases.en: I went to bed late last night.
phrases.nuance_ko: '어제저녁'보다 더 늦은 시간, 잠자기 전을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a later time than '어제저녁', closer to bedtime.

phrases.en: My stomach has hurt since last evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어제저녁에 시작해서 지금까지 이어지는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something that started last evening and continues now.

phrases.en: I met my friend at six o'clock yesterday evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구체적인 시간과 함께 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used together with a specific time.

explain_en: Standard full form, neutral, usable in any register. '어젯밤' feels like late hours close to bedtime, while '어제저녁' suits an earlier time, around dinner. You can add '에' after it or leave it out. You will also often see it written with a space, as '어제 저녁'.

t90.ax: Last evening it rained a lot.

examples.ko: 재워 둔 돼지갈비를 오늘 저녁에 구워 먹어요.
examples.en: We'll grill the marinated pork ribs tonight.
Excuse me, two servings of pork ribs, please.
This place's pork ribs have a sweet marinade.

examples.ko: 돼지갈비에 밥도 한 공기 같이 주세요.
examples.en: With the pork ribs, please also give me a bowl of rice.
Pork ribs are cheaper than beef ribs.
I had pork ribs for lunch, so I'm full.

explain: 돼지고기의 갈비 부분을 양념해 구워 먹는 음식을 말해요. '소갈비'와 달리 돼지고기라서 값이 보통 더 부담 없어요. 불판에 구워 상추에 싸 먹는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: I grill pork ribs on the grill.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고기를 불에 익히는 동작을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the action of cooking meat over heat.

phrases.en: The marinated pork ribs are delicious.
phrases.nuance_ko: 양념에 재운 돼지갈비를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to pork ribs soaked in seasoning.

phrases.en: I had dinner at a pork rib restaurant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돼지갈비를 파는 식당을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A restaurant that serves pork ribs.

explain_en: It refers to marinated pork ribs, usually grilled. Unlike '소갈비' (beef ribs), it is pork, so it is usually the cheaper choice. People often grill it at the table and wrap it in lettuce.
